correctness.rationale: Reconstructed all definitions and quantifiers: T_i starts after exit and is positive with finite mean. The Laplace occupation transform gives exactly R_s(ii)=[1+a_i E integral_0^T_i exp(-u/s)du]^-1. Its denominator strictly increases in every s>0, and its limits are 1 and pi_i, even when the chain is nonnormal. As R_s is nonnegative stochastic and C_h=2R_{h/2}-I, each state has at most one 1/2 crossing and the global positivity set is exactly [0,h_*]. A finite geometric matrix inverse proves the directed-cycle root and n-limit with no unstated spectral assumptions. Exact-fraction verifier independently cross-checks the killed-generator first-return transform and matrix resolvent on nine generators; no finite test stands in for an infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: The closest full-text published result proves the one-interval threshold only under reversibility and states nonreversible positivity windows are unclassified. The new regenerative first-return identity proves all diagonal resolvents strictly decrease for every finite irreducible nonreversible generator, closing this specific gap and giving exact directed-cycle thresholds. Searches found no statement implying the new nonreversible theorem; specialist literature may still contain it, so publication priority remains an identified risk.

value.rationale: The existing fixed-generator reversible theorem explicitly left nonreversible reentrant positivity unresolved. A universal no-reentrance classification over all finite irreducible CTMC generators is a structurally motivated theorem for numerical propagation on directed networks, replacing a symmetry-restricted spectral argument by an explicit regenerative occupation identity. The cycle threshold gives a natural complete directed family with an exact three-state golden-ratio value and dimension-dependent limit. This is a meaningful extension of applicability, not a routine known-table recomputation or an artificial parameter slice.
